newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares start week mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares start week mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares started the week mixed in quiet trade described by brokers as typical Monday dealings.
"It was typically Monday trade, slow and quiet. Nothing much happened except for a few losses and some gains," one broker said.
Among the losers, finance house UDC dropped 25 cents to 215, while pork processor Colcom, packaging firm Hunyani and building group Mash each shed 10 cents to 310, 370 and 140 respectively.

Winners included plastics investor IHL, which surged 300 cents to 4,500 and finance group Finhold, which rose 50 cents to 1,050. Discount house DCZ and tea and coffee producer Eastern Highlands each put on 15 cents to 155 and 140 respectively, while tobacco company TSL added 10 cents to 570.
Other counters were largely unchanged and the 57-share industrial index edged up 1.83 points to close at 6,992.15.
In minings, gold producer Ashanti leapt 200 cents to 15,700, but Falgold dropped 15 cents to 160 and Wankie Colliery shed 10 cents to 350.
The seven-counter mining index put on 11.75 points to 1,374.82.
